We returned to Hotel28 Myeongdong in June for our fourth consecutive year — it truly feels like our second home whenever we visit Seoul.

From the moment we step inside, the ground-floor team makes us feel warmly welcomed. Sanghoon Lee, the security officer, greeted us cheerfully every morning and was always quick to help us catch a taxi. Nicole was equally efficient with transportation, and Mathias kindly ensured the elevator was ready for us — a thoughtful gesture we especially appreciated when carrying heavy bags.

The exceptional service continues upstairs at reception. Amanda, Patrick, Sia, Jinny, and May consistently greet guests with bright smiles and go out of their way to assist. Whether we needed directions, efficient travel advice, or help planning our days around Seoul, they were always ready and genuinely caring. Amanda, with her bright smile and sweet personality that instantly lifts your spirits, even helped us book haircut appointments at Juno Hair, just around the corner from the hotel. Patrick also went above and beyond by helping us extend our stay for an extra day because we were enjoying it so much.

The location is unbeatable. Just steps from the vibrant Myeongdong shopping street and surrounded by excellent restaurants, the hotel is only a short walk from the subway station. Lotte Department Store and Shinsegae Department Store are conveniently accessible through the underground shopping center near the subway entrance, making everything feel effortlessly close. As a charming boutique seven-floor property, it’s wonderfully easy to come and go. We also appreciated the 24/7 laundry facility, which proved incredibly convenient during our longer stay.

Thoughtful extras made our visit even better: a discount card offering 15% off at nearby restaurants, shops, cafes, and a  pharmacy (we happily used it at Din Tai Fung on the second floor), and a fridge stocked daily with complimentary drinks and snack — Coke, juice, soju, beer, water, and almonds. It was so nice to return to the hotel after a long day and have something cold to drink waiting for us.

If you’re looking for a comfortable, perfectly located hotel with genuinely caring staff in the heart of Myeongdong, look no further. Hotel28 Myeongdong has earned our loyalty year after year — we’ll definitely be back for our fifth visit!

I can thoroughly recommend room 2023 and would stay in that room again if we came back to Seoul. The hotel also has four lifts which made getting up and down to the room very quick and easy with hardly any waiting.

The hotel is very central, so the pedestrianised streets nearby can be quite busy with tourists, particularly at the weekend. We enjoyed the buzz of it, and it meant there were lots of shops, restaurants and in the evening street food stalls very close by. Getting to other parts of the city was very easy as they were either walkable in 20-25 minutes or you could easily get a subway from Myeongdong Station, usually with a maximum of one change of line.

I would definitely recommend this hotel, which we found to be good value and an extremely pleasant stay.

This was my first experience in Seoul, indeed in South Korea and Le Meridien is an excellent choice for both location and comfort. As I am sure most of you know, Incheon airport is a long way outside Seoul and will take around 45 minutes to drive - maybe more if the traffic is bad. The hotel arranged a very nice car to pick us up since we were arriving from a long trans-pacific from Minneapolis. We appreciated how efficient both the pick up in particular, and the airport in general turned out to be. 

If, as we did, you arrive by car/taxi, you will be dropped in a basement-like area which necessitates heading up a couple of floors, by elevator, to reception to check in. It works very well and for those of us who sadly don't speak Korean, the helpful staff at the desk speak excellent english. We are elite Bonvoy members which always helps at Marriott properties (and secures you access to free ice cream at reception here!) and gives you a higher floor for your room and also access to the lounge which is a very worthwhile perk. We took breakfast there and it has good views over Seoul.

The rooms themselves are clean, very modern in design and thoughtfully put together. The beds in Marriotts are universally excellent in my experience and here is no exception. Large beds, firmish mattress and crisp extremely comfortable linens. As we found throughout our travels in Asia, ensuite bathrooms at this level of hotel have not only a large walk in shower but also a soaking tub which is something I greatly enjoy and hugely miss in my travels within the US where a bathtub is generally absent from hotel rooms - unless you count the pathetic shower over shallow tub that seemed to be de rigeur in the 70s and 80s and persists in many places to this day. This is to be highly commended.

We were only here for two nights and so were unable to sample the other facililies such as the gym and the swimming pool but being a full service hotel these looked very nice too. The location is great. We went on a walking tour from the hotel our only full day here and were able to walk out from the lobby to some of the main attractions in Seoul which makes it an excellent choice especially if you are only here for a short time. Our trip was essentially a 48 hour layover before heading over to China. Would definitely stay here again.

소개: GLAD Hotel is the first member hotel of 'Design Hotels' in Seoul. GLAD Hotel Yeouido is conveniently located right outside of Exit 4 of National Assembly Subway Station (Line 9) and offers a 24-hour access fitness centre. Property-wide WiFi access and on-site parking are available for free. Featuring a minibar, each room is fitted with a work desk, seating area and 42 inch LED TV with cable and satellite channels. Private bathroom comes with Kudos bathroom amenities. 24-hour front desk and free shuttle services are available at GLAD Hotel Yeouido. From the hotel, Korean National Assembly Complex is a 5-minute walk and IFC Mall is a 15-minute walk away. The hotel is a 25-minute drive from Gimpo Airport and a 50-minute drive from Incheon International Airport. In the glimmering skyscraper-filled district of Yeouido, aptly nicknamed Seoul's Manhattan, GLAD Hotel Yeouido is already turning things on its head. The hotel's facade, with its unusual brick pattern, at once stands out from its neighbors' modernist glass buildings. Bricks have also been wittily used in the hotel's interiors. And to create an "on the street" experience, street signs help guide you home to your room. Thanks to an honest approach to design, rooms are cozy and practical with no hidden or confusing features, and the hotel's Greets restaurant and cafe revels in natural materials and pure forms. Bar Mark T, inspired by Mark Twain's favorite tipple, serves up the city's most extensive and unique collection of Single Malt Whiskey. The cozy rooms feature practical open shelving for storage, desk space, and even a lounge sofa for relaxing. High quality natural materials give the spaces a sense of calm and warmth. Posters in each room play on the hotel's 'glad' motif with amusing quotes from renowned thinkers such as Eleanor Roosevelt and Shakespeare. A local type of brick was chosen as the dominant structural material to give GLAD Hotel Yeouido the warmth and soul of a traditional South Korean home. But thanks to award-winning Joh & Company's singular vision, the bricks are expressed throughout the property in unique stacking patterns. The brutalist-interiors are rendered light thanks to a playful use of the material, giving depth and texture to the lobby. The hotel also adheres to the national environment-friendly standard and proudly uses geothermal energy.

I’ve stayed in several hotels in Mapo over the years for work, and the Roynet is easily the best choice. What really sets it apart is the ability to control the room temperature yourself, something that’s surprisingly hard to find in Seoul. Many hotels claim to offer in-room controls, but in reality they rely on a central system, which often results in overly warm and stuffy rooms during winter.
The Roynet feels modern, clean, and well thought out. It offers practical amenities such as a free coffee corner, an ice machine, and self-service laundry. The rooms are comfortable and functional, with good beds, power outlets on both sides, blackout curtains, and dimmable lighting.
If you’re not in the mood for a Korean breakfast at the hotel restaurant, there’s a convenient Western-style alternative at A Twosome Place on the ground floor beneath the hotel. Overall, I would definitely recommend the Roynet as the preferred option when staying in Mapo

We stayed for five nights recently and had an excellent stay. We had a two-bedroom unit with well equipped full kitchen and living room that gave us a lot of room, especially for Seoul.  It's true that there are some dings in the furniture and baseboards and the carpet in master bedroom was a little worn (otherwise had wood floors in the unit) but we didn't think this was a big deal. The unit was clean with a lot of closet and drawer space, safe that could accommodate laptops, good size bathroom with double vanity, separate tub and shower and toilet with bidet function, washer and dryer combo in the unit (though drying function was quite slow). Breakfast buffet as noted is a little repetitive--scrambled eggs with some kind of potato, bacon and sausage, breads, cereal, cut apples, banana, oranges every day. Generally well done but it's true that most of the breakfast could be found almost anywhere.  However, soup and one dish varied each day (e.g. lasagna, pasta with bolognese sauce, one day Korean fried chicken). Weekends had an additional Korean dish (e.g. kimchi jigae) that was welcome--would be nice if there were more Korean or Asian dishes. 

Excellent location in Insadong area, lots of shops within walking distance with a focus on Korean arts and crafts, calligraphy brushes, pottery. 7-11 across the street from the front of the hotel and a well-stocked supermarket about a three minute walk away (turn left out the front door of the hotel, it is next to the Amid Hotel). We walked to Myeongdong,  Gyeongbukgung palace and Bukchon Hanok Village--all about a 20 minute walk away--but the hotel is close to several subway stations as well (closest would probably be Jongno 3-ga Station). Staff professional and eager to please. Certainly there are less expensive alternatives, but hard to beat if you are looking for more room, and something more like an apartment in Seoul.

리뷰_2:
We are a family of four (two adults and two late teens) and stayed in a Family Twin room (two queen beds) for six nights, with breakfast included for two people.
The room had sufficient space for all of us and our luggage. It included an armchair, a small table, and a work desk with a chair. The beds were comfortable, although the pillows were quite soft—we ended up using two each. The bathtub design was a bit unusual, as water tended to spill over the sides when showering. There were two USB ports (one by the bedside and one at the worktable) and two power outlets, which were originally for the lamps but we used them to charge our devices.
We appreciated the small welcome gift—it was a nice touch. Four bottles of water were replenished daily, and housekeeping kept the room clean throughout our stay.
Breakfast was only included for two people, but since we were staying for six nights, we asked if our family of four could have breakfast every second day instead (three breakfasts total). Although reception initially said this wouldn’t be possible at check-in, the restaurant manager kindly accommodated our request. Thank you, Charles—we really appreciated being able to enjoy breakfast together as a family. The breakfast itself was great—we especially loved the fresh croffles, and the coffee was good. A slightly wider selection of Western-style hot food would have made it even better, but overall it was a very enjoyable experience.
We used the laundry facility (washing machine and dryer) regularly - 3k won and there’s a change machine.
Getting an Uber usually took 10 minutes or more, and pickup was at the Ibis Ambassador next door. This became frustrating on checkout day when we needed to get to Seoul Station for our train to Busan—we couldn’t get an UberXL and had to squeeze into a regular Uber with all our luggage.
The location was excellent—close to eateries, shops, public transport, the cathedral, and major sightseeing spots. Next time, we might try staying in Insadong or Hongdae for a different experience.

리뷰_1:
Like many other guests have noted, Four Points by Sheraton Seoul Myeongdong offers many features that make international travelers feel comfortable and welcome. The location is excellent, the views are impressive, the rooms are quiet, the beds are comfortable, and the staff members are professional and attentive. These qualities alone make it a property that I would gladly recommend. However, I would like to highlight an additional feature that most guests may not notice but can certainly benefit from—indoor air quality.

As an indoor air quality researcher, I travel with laboratory-grade air quality instruments and routinely assess hotel guestrooms around the world. During my three-night stay in Room #2607, I monitored carbon dioxide (CO₂) levels, which are commonly used as an indicator of fresh-air ventilation effectiveness in occupied spaces. I was pleasantly surprised to find that overnight CO₂ levels generally remained around or below 800 ppm while I was sleeping. Research has shown that maintaining bedroom CO₂ concentrations below approximately 800 ppm can support better sleep quality by reducing sleep disturbances and nighttime awakenings. In many hotels I have assessed, overnight CO₂ levels frequently exceed 1,500 to 2,000 ppm, particularly in tightly sealed guestrooms.

The ventilation system in Room #2607 continuously supplied fresh outdoor air throughout the night, helping maintain a healthy sleeping environment. As someone who often struggles with severe jet lag during international travel, I found that I slept exceptionally well during my stay. While guests may choose this hotel for its location, comfort, and service, I believe the property's effective fresh-air ventilation deserves recognition as an additional amenity that contributes to guest wellness and restorative sleep. I hope hotel management continues to invest in and promote this often-overlooked aspect of the guest experience.

I would happily stay here again on my next visit to Seoul.

리뷰_3:
The hotel: This was the perfect choice for my first time in Seoul. After doing my research reading through many reviews on different forums, I chose FS due to it's location and reputation for wonderful service. The building is easy to spot and very close to the bus and train station. I arrived very early to this hotel based on my flight schedule from the states, and unfortunately I was not able to check-in early. A small criticism - I was never notified my room was ready (but I already went about my day and dropped my bags off with the bell staff, so a non-issue). Once I was ready to check-in, staff communicated expertly in English and were helpful.

The room: I booked a club level, double-bed room. In all honesty, barring the lobby, the hotel is really designed for corporate travelers. I would have loved to see more cultural flair, but it's very business aesthetic. Having said that, the views are incredible, with floor-to-ceiling windows. All appliances were functional, and plenty of space for two travelers. The room was very clean and housekeeping provided daily turndown service. There were no wifi issues during my visit. My mom enjoyed the sitting ledge in the shower after long walking days.

Club lounge: This was a real perk during my stay. The lounge had very friendly and accommodating staff. Breakfast had a nice selection of dishes (pastries, regional food, meats, cheeses etc.). The afteroon had a nice tea break. It was great to pop in during the day for a nice respite from sightseeing. The lounge never felt busy or rushed, which I really appreciated.

Onsite Restaurants: The breakfast buffet at the Market kitchen is extensive. I'd recommend visiting at least one day to try all the different dishes out. My mom and I visited Maru for afternoon tea. What a delight! Each pastry and small dish was expertly crafted and tasted delicious. I only wish there were more tea selections, but it was a lovely way to spend an afternoon. I dined at Boccalino one night for dinner. The restaurant design is beautiful. While the food was good, I wasn't quite blown away, and there are many other options to dine elsewhere. Charles H. bar is a definite must-do. The cocktails are terrific and so are the small dishes.

Staff: Staff really did shine here. I never encountered any language barriers and they always seemed appreciative of the few Korean words I spoke :) Concierge was able to accomodate any dining request I had. Someone would always say hello and smile whenever I walked through the lobby.

The area: This hotel is in an excellent location. The airport bus stop is right across the street. Numerous other bus lines also run by the hotel. The Line 5 train is right around the hotel. The trains and buses were easy to use (but I also say this as a NYer with bus and train experience back home). There are palaces and shopping/dining within walking distance.

Summary:
+ Clean
+ Great area
- Can be expensive
- Designed for business travelers

리뷰_1:
My wife and I stayed here for 5 nights in room 1712, the/an Ambassador Suite.

We took bus 6702 from the airport to the hotel. It took 2.5 hours, 18,000won, as the bus called at other hotels and the Ambassador was the last stop. The bus had to wait at several hotels near the end for a scheduled departure time in case passengers were returning to the airport. However, on return to the airport it took 1 hour 35 minutes as the hotel was 6th pick up. If you are using the bus to get to the hotel then it is best to get off at Jangchung Gymnasium from where the hotel will be about 5 minutes walk. It could save you 30 minutes or more.

Check in had to be done in 18th floor as I had booked lounge access.

ROOM
Comprised an entrance hall with toilet, sitting area with sofa, easy chair, table and 2 chairs, fridge, tea/coffee facilities, tv. The bedroom had lounge chair, dressing table, tv. There was masses of storage space.  The bedroom gave access to a walk-in wardrobe with safe, storage for cases, drawers and an area with 2 sinks. There was no iron/board but these were supplied on request.

BATHROOM
This comprised a room with 3 showers (2 wall-mounted and 1 overhead), a room with a toilet and in between them a bath in solitary isolation. There were large dispensers for toiletries. A small charge was made for a dental kit and a shaving kit.
The WC was automatic and when the door to the cubicle was opened the toilet seat rose up. The seat was warm and flushing was automatic. It seemed to have a mind of its own and flushed sometimes too soon. A bit off putting sometimes!
I tried twice to have a bath and found the water not sufficiently hot for comfort. However, the water in the shower was hot and efficient.

LOUNGE ACCESS
Breakfast was delicious with a huge choice of fresh salads, pastries, noodles, cooked dishes, fruit, yoghurt, cereals etc. There was a large coffee/tea making machine. Omelettes could be cooked to order. It was very quiet when we were there. Breakfast can also be eaten on 1st floor (ground) restaurant but we preferred the lounge.

The lounge is open throughout the day with soft drinks, tea/coffee and cookies always available.

Access included afternoon tea which was a stand with 4 savoury items and 6 sweet cakes. We enjoyed these with a cup of tea!

Dinner had a fantastic selection of hot and cold dishes, cheese, desserts and fruit. The dishes were exceptionally high quality and delicious. However, the dishes never changed from day to day and it would have been good to have a “daily special” type dish. The hot dishes were not particularly a hot temperature. E.g. chips were lukewarm. We have eaten in other lounges around the world and this is the best we have experienced in terms of choice and quality. Drinks were free, and included wine, spirits and cocktails.

We were given a voucher for a free drink in the bar on the 1st floor. It was surprising that water was not included in the choice.

The hotel is about a 3 minute walk from a Metro station (Dongguk University) and so easy for exploring Seoul.

I thoroughly recommend this hotel. We had a really marvellous stay and thoroughly enjoyed the food and comfort. All the staff were unfailingly polite and helpful.

What drew me to this hotel was its location next to Seoul Station, so you can really go anywhere from there. The hotel and station is easily accessible from the B2 basement floor - great if you want to stay out of the sun. 
I also liked that the hotel has coin laundry. I knew I'd need it as I was staying for over two weeks - the instructions were clear and helpful, and their coin machine meant I didn't have to worry about making change or breaking large bills at convenience stores. But if I had to, there is a store right next door - the staff there too were lovely.

A real high point was the breakfast. They had everything: hot and cold breakfast, fruits and yogurt or pastries, or sausages, bacon, eggs or salads and hams. And more. They also had juices and of course coffee. The breakfast room was also kept very clean and there was staff on hand if you needed help. 

All in all, as a solo traveler who was a bit nervous about the trip, I'm so glad I picked this hotel. It's worth the money and gave me great peace of mind. 리뷰_2: Located at the heart of bukchon hanok village, this hanok hotel boasts great views of the village and namsan tower from its vantage point. It combines the charms of the traditional hanok house with great service and modern comforts — from helping us to take our luggages to our room, to little touches such as the welcome tea, complimentary hanbok wearing experience, snacks bar, sheet masks and in room coffee machine. 리뷰_3: A beautiful tranquil hanok in Bukchon Hanok Village. Very kind, responsive and accommodating staff.  Loved the amenities and breakfast delivered to my room. Close to a number of cafes and restaurants yet very peaceful. Such a unique experience, especially for a Westerner first time in Seoul.
리뷰_4:
We stayed for three nights and loved the experience of being in a traditional Korean house. We were slightly concerned before arriving that we might find the beds too hard and would have difficulty sleeping. Once we tried them we realised this was not a problem at all - it seems there are specially-designed foam layers underneath the traditional mats. You do need to be able to get down to floor level and back up again. For us, this was not a problem and we slept very well every night. The place is really peaceful and the service on arriving and for meals was of an exceptionally high standard. We ordered traditional Korean food for breakfast and dinner (two nights only) and it was always delicious. 

This was all perfect for us, but it might be the wrong choice for some people. You have to remove shoes while inside, which can be uncomfortable if you are used to orthotic support. The furnishings are traditional and therefore not as plush as a regular hotel. The buildings are raised and the steps up and down are steep (as they are in all old areas of Seoul). A few concessions were made for the modern traveller - coffee machine with extra pods on request, small TV hidden in the cupboard, face masks, modern bathroom - all of which we appreciated (though did not use the TV). 

On the whole, this is a most interesting traditional experience, much more than a hotel, and the staff were wonderful and extremely helpful. Our only regret about staying here is that we were out seeing the sights every day and did not have more time in the quiet and beautiful environment, and did not take advantage of the sauna and other options available on site.

The name Rakkojae means “a place to enjoy the old and rest the soul,” reflecting a philosophy of quiet elegance and cultural immersion. Each hanok presents a distinct expression of Korean architectural heritage, united by harmony with nature and traditional ways of living. Courtyards, gardens, and open wooden structures invite light, wind, and stillness, recalling the refined lifestyle of scholars and noble families. While preserving historical character, the hanoks offer modern comfort and thoughtful hospitality. Guests may enjoy curated cultural experiences such as Korean tea ceremonies, hanbok, and moments of calm rarely found in the city. On my wife's 60th birthday trip, I stayed at Conrad Seoul for two nights starting June 17.

As it was a late arrival at Gimpo airport at 22:20, we contacted the hotel in advance, but received a polite reply immediately. And, considering that this is my wife's important 60th birthday celebration trip, we upgraded it to an executive river view room.

After check-in, the couple entered the room and were deeply moved by the beautiful Han River scenery and the heartwarming message of "Happy 60th Birthday" on the window along with the birthday cake. It was the first such wonderful surprise and a memory I will never forget.

We even arranged for the executive lounge guests to book a spot at the popular Chango 43 Yeouijima Main Store, where they could enjoy a wonderful dinner.

Afternoon tea and evening cocktails were served in the executive lounge. In particular, Taylor Kim and the rest of the executive lounge team were very kind to me, and I have great memories of having fun conversations and taking pictures with them during my stay. Furthermore, after returning to Japan, we even received a heartwarming e-mail, which both the couple were deeply moved by.

As a Hilton Diamond member, I have stayed at many Hilton affiliated hotels both in Japan and abroad, and my stay at Conrad Seoul was definitely top class. Not only are the facilities luxurious and the views stunning, but the staff's warm hospitality and attention to detail have left a lasting impression on me.

I was able to celebrate my wife's 60th birthday, an important milestone in my life, in the best way possible. Thanks to everyone at Conrad Soul, it was a wonderful memory that I will never forget.

When I visit Seoul, I would love to stay there again.

When it comes to rooms, service, and location, this hotel is phenomenal. It is located on top of the shopping mall. It is opposite an absolutely amazing temple. It is in the heart of Gangnam. It is very modern, recently refurbished, extremely clean, with amazing staff and great service for staff. The fitness centre is to die for. Seriously, one of the best fitness centres I've ever seen in a hotel, with an amazing pool. Because the fitness centre is open to the public, it is also extremely well run, and I actually like a little bit of a crowd in the fitness centre because it's got a bit of a vibe, so very impressed on that front.
The club lounge, if you can go to it, is also phenomenal, with a great view from the 30th floor.
If I was to give you some negatives, they are fairly minor ones:
1. There is a phenomenal number of little things in the room that emit light. Even the toilet has a light on it, so in my bedtime routine I had to spend a lot of time trying to eliminate and cover them all up.
2. While it has lots of lifts (there are six of them), they sneak up on you. They are very quiet, so often I would find that the lift doors were shutting because I hadn't realised they had even opened up.
3. The rooms have been completely refurbished, but the shower door opens inwards, which means that you either need to get in the shower before turning it on or play a rather interesting game of trying to turn on the shower and then get into the shower with the shower running on you. I just don't like that design. I understand that they did it because it was the best way to use space, but it is effectively a poor design.

Either way, this is a phenomenal hotel, and I highly recommend it.

I had room 305 and it was very comfortable. Although I travelled solo it would have been fine for a couple.  The bed was comfy and the bathroom clean with a powerfull shower.  There were two comfy chairs and a table also a computer but I could not get it to work in English. There were no wardrobes but I only had a small suitcase so this did not bother me.  The wifi was excellent. The hotel staff were very pleasant and helpful.
The airport limousine bus 6011 stops very close to the hotel. Just get off at the Changdeokgung palace stop (it is the stop after Anguk) and you will see the hotel is just ahead on your right. Take the first turning on the right down a narrow street and the hotel will be on the left a little way down. Airport bus is 10000 won and was equivalent to about 7 GBP and is a fast and comfortable way to get to the city.
The hotel serves a breakfast as an extra but I used the small shop just outside the hotel where you can get a hot coffee and a snack at very cheap prices if you are on a budget. Tables and chairs are provided to sit outside if the weather is nice.
Hotel is in a good place to explore being close to both palaces and also the Insa-dong area where there are shops and places to eat.  It appeared to be a very safe area to me as an older British woman travelling alone.  I would stay there again.  
I also had a nice day in the Bukhansan national park which was easy to get to by tube and bus from Anguk.  
I had  two nights with two full days in Seoul as a stopover on my way to Japan and thoroughly enjoyed it, I would like to see more of South Korea next time.

I had a great stay at Voco Seoul Gangnam by IHG. The location is fantastic — just a 5-minute walk from Sinsa Station, and there’s almost everything you need right around the hotel. There’s a UNIQLO right across the street, plus KFC, coffee shops, pharmacies, and even a 24-hour restaurant nearby, which made my stay super convenient.

The room was clean, the bed was very comfortable, and the bathroom was spotless. Room service is available until 11 PM daily, which is a nice plus. My only small disappointment was that the in-room dining menu didn’t offer many Korean food options.

Housekeeping overall was good, and the lady who cleaned my room was very friendly and kind. I did notice that there were a few pieces of garbage under the bed, so attention to detail in that area could be improved slightly.

I also appreciated how thoughtful the staff were. On the first day when I did not request cleaning service, they hung a bag of fresh towels and bottled water on my door, which was perfect. However, on the second day, I returned from lunch and found four new bottles of water placed on the minibar table and my towels replaced — even though my “Do Not Disturb” light was still on. I understand the intention was to provide fresh supplies, which I appreciate, but it would have been better if the front desk had called to confirm before entering the room.

One more highlight: my floor had a shared public kitchen where guests can cook or microwave food, which I think is a great feature, especially for longer stays.

Overall, despite the small issues, I really enjoyed my stay and would definitely consider coming back.

We had 2 rooms - each with 2 double beds overlooking the City Hall ‘lawn’.  We checked in at the 5th floor member reception and our bags were quickly delivered to the rooms.  Our rooms were inexpensive and they were rather tight but were well appointed and there was plenty of storage space and excellent AC.  The beds were on the firm side, but bedding was excellent.  Bathroom was small but had decent vanity space, a good rain shower and fancy programmable toilet (we’ll miss that when we leave Asia!!)
We had CNN and BBC to watch!
The Lounge on the 5th floor was a real advantage - great breakfast and evening meal/appetizers. The Plaza team was truly the highlight of this stay; Callum particularly was so helpful.  He checked us in and then helped me order and take delivery of a  ($12) TENS machine (my husband pinched a nerve in his neck 4 days earlier and his left arm was numb/painful).  It was delivered to our room the following evening - worked a treat.  
Callum helped with everything we needed or asked for and everyone at the hotel was incredibly respectful, polite and kind.  We were really blown away by the Korean culture and the vibe in the city.
The Gyeongbokgung Palace is a 20minute walk away and well worth the trip - beautiful complex! 
We visited on the day Korea played Mexico in round 1 of the World Cup.  There was a huge street watch party which we joined briefly. Mexico won 1-0 in the end, but the crowd was upbeat, respectful and calm even in defeat.  Some other nations could take note ….
Shopping is 15mins to the SE of the hotel and there are Starbucks and 7-11 stores on virtually every street corner so you’re never in need!!! You can also connect to many areas via the underground tunnels which can be accessed directly below the hotel.
It was a wonderful 3 day visit and we’d definitely come back again - not least for the incredible and highly consistent customer service.

I stayed at the Hotel Thomas Myeongdong for 5 nights. The hotel is modern, well-maintained, and has a rather new appearance. Check-in is done independently through the automatic kiosks, but we were assisted by the friendly staff who are always present at the reception.
The room was spacious and well-organized, with enough space to comfortably open and arrange 23 kg suitcases. The bathroom was not particularly large, but it was functional. I really appreciated the provided bathroom products, including high-quality shampoo, conditioner, and body cream.
The view from the room, despite being on the tenth floor, faced another building and was therefore not particularly interesting. The beds were very comfortable, the TV was large, and there was also a practical desk. Cleaning was done every day with care. Water was always available in the room.
Its location is excellent: it is in a quiet area but at the same time very convenient, with restaurants and bars nearby. In fact, we found a really great restaurant just a few meters from the hotel, and there is a 7-Eleven very close to the building. Moreover, the property is very close to both Seoul Plaza, where the Limousine Airport Bus stop is located, and Myeongdong, which is easily reachable on foot.
One service that we particularly appreciated was the ability to leave our luggage at the hotel for free during the four days we spent outside of Seoul. 
Overall, I recommend the Hotel Thomas Myeongdong, a modern, well-located, and comfortable establishment!

The hotel is very near Yeoksam Station in Gangnam-gu and there was a taxi rank on Teheran-ro so getting around was very easy. 1) Location: It's a good location, only about 5-minutes walking distance to the conference center and the botanic park is only a stroll away. The park is small but it's nice. There are enough shops and restaurants also if for your needs. I found the location is nice for the good night sleep because it's so quiet and peaceful at night.

The interior has some "earth" tone colors as this hotel adopting eco-friendly model. It blends really well with the green space such as Botanic Park. The room has water filtration system for drinking, coffee machine, and also equipped with air purifier system. The bathroom also has a decent space, not very cramped. The toilet seat may be intimidating to use as it has a lot of buttons, but honestly it's not that hard to use. Bedding is very comfortable. Overall, it's one of the nicest Courtyard room. 

4) Garden Kitchen: Breakfast served at the Garden Kitchen. Honestly it was pretty modest. Options are good, but they tasted bland. The coffee from the machine also taste average. Definitely a room for improvement. 

Overall, it was a wonderful stay for me. There was a bit of incident happen, but Ms. Olivia Moon and the housekeeping manager manage to handle the incident very well. I really appreciate their effort to keep their guest happy. I will coming back if I have another chance to visit the area.

I picked it primarily because it offered the convenience of being close to the metro line I needed to get to my conference. I also like staying at Bonvoy hotels when I can, so I was able to enjoy benefits like late check out. It was an excellent value for my week long stay. As a first timer in Seoul, I also really liked staying in Gangnam. It felt very comfortable, while still offering easy access to some of the more popular tourist spots. There are plenty of options for great food, coffee and shopping mere steps away. While my room was on the smaller side for what I usually get, it was definitely spacious enough for one. It was also modern, clean, and comfortably equipped. The 24/7 fitness was also decent and nice to have as an option. Staff were all friendly, too. I occasionally had trouble getting the right temperature but that’s probably more on me. I would recommend the hotel and I wouldn’t hesitate staying there again. I stayed at the Hotel Amare Jongno for 7 nights from April 19 and overall the experience was more than positive, despite having read some negative reviews before departure, especially related to the hotel's reputation as a love hotel which is absolutely not true.
Upon arrival we asked for a room with a bathroom a little more reserved having read and seen the photos of this too, and the staff was immediately available to change the room with one that would better meet our needs. The room was very spacious, bathroom with shower and bath, we found supplied in addition to the usual bath foam, shampoo and conditioner also body cream, lotion and essence for the face, several brushes great for every need for hair and hairdryer. There is also a terrace from where you can see the Namsan tower.
I liked the breakfast although purely salty but I loved the toast with butter and jam. The really convenient location to explore Seoul, especially the Insadong area and surroundings. Yes, in the evening there are drunk people around but unfortunately they are not only in this area and we were never bothered by anyone indeed, the area I liked also because it was not at all touristy but close to everything.
The less positive aspects were the not perfect cleaning on some surfaces and the plasticized crossbar in the bed that made me sweat but after moving it I could not find it anymore so the cleaners will have understood the discomfort. The view was on a semi-abandoned building but returning only in the evening to sleep what is the view for?
However, overall we enjoyed it and would recommend it, especially for those looking for a central and comfortable accommodation at a reasonable price.

리뷰_1: Stayed here in Oct 2014 for 6 nights by myself as a single woman.   I wanted a safe budget accommodations under $80 that was clean with a frig, microwave and washer, an ensuite bathroom and free wifi.  My room also had a window.  It was nicely decorated.  This place was pretty self-sufficient.  The manager at the front desk (a young man) speaks fluent English and very helpful.  He used to live a couple of years in California.  The cleaning lady doesn't come to your room daily to clean it.   If you want your garbage emptied, bed made or bathroom clean, you need to request it from the front desk.   Since I didn't want anyone to come into the room, I just put a used shopping bag in the garbage can in my room.  When it got full,  I just emptied it out on the public garbage can on the 2nd floor.  I had a double room.  This place was a perfect fit for me.    It might be a little cramp for 2 people who need a lot of space.   The only thing I wasn't used to was that if you wanted to take a shower, the shower is above the toilet.  To keep the toilet seat from getting wet, you need to cover the seat with the lid.  Ventilation was really fast so I got used to it.  I loved the place.  From Incheon International Airport, you buy a $15USD or 15,000 won (Korean currency) ticket to get on airport shuttle (Bus 6009) to Sinsa bus stop.  It takes approximately 1 hour.  The airport shuttle arrives right across the street from the hotel.  It drops you off in the middle median of a 2 way street.  After you get off at Sinsa bus stop and get your suitcases, face the shuttle that just dropped u off.  Let it go by.  The hotel is directly across the street, facing you and not behind you.  You need to walk across the street to get to it.  You are approx. 2 minutes from the airport shuttle bus stop to the hotel.  This information is really important if u arrive in the night...  The hotel is up the hill between the Citibank ATM and a Car Sales Place.  The hotel is really convenient since it is within 5 minutes walk to Sinsa subway station (exit 3).  It takes approximately 20 mins to most attractions.  I did not feel threatened or unsafe while I was in Korea.  I always walked among people.  I ventured out at night since Korea's night life was filled with people.  A few places I saw that were really interesting were  (1) Bukchon Hanok Village (closest metro: Anguk Station, exit 2) for authentic style architecture of people's homes, (2) Myeongdong, a pedestrian walking area to one of Seoul’s most famous shopping districts (closest metro: Myeong-dong, Exit 8).  While you are in this area, you must eat at Myeongdong Kyoja for dumplings and handmade noodles.  It's their specialty and costs approx. $8 per person.  Similar to Japan or Harrod, you can find a huge eating world in the larger malls on the basement levels.  I suggest you check out Lotteria Mall's basement (closest metro: Jamsil exit 3) at 11am to be amazed by the amount of food and choices for every taste and budget.  In case you need to talk to someone in English, Japanese or Chinese to ask for directions or information about a place, dial 1330 for the Travel Hotline. It is a free service for tourists.  I found it really useful and helpful since I didn't speak Korean.    When it is time to leave, you don't take the same direction airport shuttle you arrived.  The airport shuttle bus going back to the airport is down the street from the hotel (away from Sinsa metro station) on the median of the bus stop.  Find on the bus signs for #6009.  You can pay 15,000 won directly to the machine in the airport shuttle.  Again, it will take approx. 1 hour to Incheon International Airport.  Allow enough time to get there before your flight.  I had a great time in Korea.  As long as you smile, say thank you (kam-sa-ham-nee-da) and hello (anyeong-haseyo),  I was fine.  Hope you have a great time in Korea too!  I can't wait to go back!

리뷰_4: First let me say that this is in fact a residence, not an hotel. You will not have a phone in the room to call the front desk and ask for more soap. In my previous visits in Seoul I stayed at the Ramada in Gangnam and at the Hotel La Casa in Sinsa. Ramada was terrible and La Casa was way too expensive for what you get. The location of the property is one of the best if you are trying to be close to the wonderful Garosu-gil shopping and dining area in Sinsa. It takes about 7 minutes walk. Sinsa station is just a short walk down the hill. The property is family owned. Kim, she speaks great English and so is her son who is often taking care of the front desk. Her husband also speaks English and he's also often around, he just doesn't speak much. Great and wonderful people, they will try their best to accommodate you. There are single, premium and deluxe doubles. Size is quite small but good enough. My friend had a single and that was way too small for me, besides, there is no washing machine in single rooms. I had a premium double but my first night I stayed in the deluxe which was just a little bigger. I liked my premium, I had microwave, a good size fridge, a small inside balcony/den where the washing machine is located. The bed is comfortable and double size. WIFI signal was good and fast enough. There is a CITIBANK just a few steps away. The good thing about this property, every room has is own A/C which you control. It's very well known that Seoul's hotels control A/Cs and shut them down whenever they please to save energy. There is no breakfast option, there is a little station on each floor with water machine, kitchen utensils, cups, glasses and so on plus a washing machine for rooms without it. There is no front desk after 7pm and you will be provided with a card to swipe to enter the property from the main or side entrance and a code to use to enter your room. If you are looking to work out, just a few blocks away there is a small but decently equipped gym which charges only $5 a day and even provides you with towels, clothes, shoes.......ask the hotel for directions to it. Solo in Asia for the first time (solo female) so here it is from that perspective. 
People say it’s hard to find which is kind of true.
There are 3 main ways to get here:

Just Train or Train/Taxi: It is really cost effective to take the train from the airport to Seoul station. Then transfer to Line 1 to continue on Trian your final station is Jongo 3 Ga - Exit 15) This will cost you around 2000W ($3 CAD)  (REMEMBER TO GET YOUR DEPOSIT BACK AT TRAIN STATION for your train cards you get 500W back each time. 

Or  Then taxi from Seoul Station (exit 1 you will find taxis) for about $10 Canadian total from airport to hotel (will take about 1hr) my taxi didn’t speak any English but even when he got into the general neighbourhood I could navigate addresses on sides of buildings to find hotel. It is tucked away in an alley between two very main busy streets (which is great) just will take you a second to find. It’s main cross street building is the YBM building.  I’m glad I didn’t bus from train station not worth it to save mere dollars when tired after flight and have luggage. 

Or Airport bus. The airport buses take 1 hr, run every 15min or so and are 10000W and you do not need to book ahead of time. These are not city buses they are charter buses. Final stop would be at Jongo 3 Station  again which is a 5min walk to hotel. 

All are options to go home with, trains/buses start running at 530am 

This hotel is in between 4 main subway lines which is great, Line 1 and 2 get you all your main places. Don’t be afraid of subway or bus it makes a lot of sense when you don’t let the different Language thing overwhelm you. It is your cheapest and easiest way to get around. If you are going to Seoul tower the 143 but takes you right there (you get off at namsam 3tunnel stop) gets your closer then train. 

Check in was under 2 minutes, easy, was in my room within 7min of being in front doors. So far most staff speak English. Housekeeping is super friendly (they provide water, and lots of little toiletries in room) The staff gave me suggestions when requested of best ways to get certain places or means back to airport (don’t use a taxi back to airport unless you have to its 65000W) 

This is not the super nice part of town but you are darn close. You want to be in Myeondung district (which this is)  This is just a touch more weatherd of an area but you are only blocks away form everything & the fancy stuff. The hotel itself is really nice but all surrounding stores/buildings are a bit older. Safe neighbourhood. I stand out like a sore thumb here but I never felt unsafe around the hotel
 711 outside front door. Lots of restaurants. Insadong market/street is only minutes away. Super central, where you want to be. Starbucks/mcdonalds/subway all minutes away. I was really happy with this location wise in the city. 
There is a traditional Korean bbq right downstairs (I don’t eat meat) but it’s full of locals every night, thats got to be good. 

There is construction in the buildings next door, starts at 7am right now (April 2018)  doesn’t bother me as I sleep with earplugs and am up at 5am because of jet lag every day. But to some that may be a bother. Looks like it will be going on for some time, but a lot of the rooms don’t face that way anyways. 

Room is nice, not the fanciest thing in the world but perfect for me. Comfy bed, and most importantly HOT water. The best hot water I have ever had in Asia. Doesn’t change temps and can shower any time or day/night with consistency. Safe in room and mini fridge. I don’t think they had AC on yet, there is a machine for it but I couldn’t seem to figure it out - I never asked as they have windows that open that let fresh air in. 

You can’t beat the price for what you are getting/location - Over all very happy, will be back if I’m around here again!

We hadn't planned to stay here, in fact we thought that we had booked the Four Points by Seoul Station but, through a combination of clicking quickly online and not paying attention, we ended up standing in the Reception of the Four Points by Seoul Station, trying to book in, when our booking had actually been made for Guro-gu -some 10 stops and a line change away on the metro!

Our initial reaction was to ask if we could transfer our booking - the two hotels are, after all, members of the same organisation; but a particularly unhelpful / reticent member of staff forced us to come to the conclusion that we would have to bite the bullet, do the journey (four suitcases between us!) and head to Guro.

This is perhaps the only 'con' of the hotel, getting to it in the first place.  The Seoul metro is pretty good for providing elevators or escalators, we only came across two sections where we had to just take a deep breath and lug our suitcases up a flight of stairs, but we were lucky to be doing this on a relatively quiet Sunday afternoon; it is not something I would like to attempt on a busy weekday.

That said, outside the hotel is a stop for the excellent Airport Limousine Bus service so, if you are coming to the hotel from the airport, this would be an option.  At the moment, there is only a limited service but, as Covid restrictions ease, the timetable should expand to it's former regular service.  It is also only about an hour's journey from the airport and, at the end of our visit, Reception staff called attaxi for us, which was a highly convenient way to  travel and very reasonably priced.

Oh what a difference, walking into the Four Points in Guro - the staff were friendly and so welcoming and, clearly seeing that we were completely drained from our journey, couldn't do enough to make check in quick and simple.

Guro is a much less urban district, wide open streets, and the hotel opens onto the pavement, set back from the road, with a huge Reception area, a Dunkin' Donuts and a Starbucks to one side and part of the hotel building.  An overall feeling of space and light, which we hadn't experienced in their sister hotel.

We had a spacious room on the 12th floor, where we could watch the traffic and people below, but were not disturbed by any noise.  A large, very comfortable bed, with a veritable mountain of pillows, a couple of armchairs and table by the window, desk and chair and wall-mounted TV above.  Plenty of charging points for tech and the power points by the bedside were universal and also had USB points within them.

The shelf for suitcases was welcome.  There was also a good sized wardrobe and drawer space, ironing board and iron, room safe and fridge with complimentary water each day.  The amenity tray had kettle, cups and glasses and a modest array of tea and coffee - there were also toothbrushes, shower cap, soap etc.

Having a bath was a real boon, as we had been staying in an apartment for seven weeks with only a shower; and we both took the opportunity to have a good soak and then relax in the complimentary bathrobes and slippers.  The bathrobes were a little snug - my other half struggled around the middle and with the length - a couple of towels each, with the bath towel passing the modesty test (I could open the door, wrapped in a towel and maintain my modesty).

Masses of hot water and a fancy toilet seat which performed all sorts of functions!

On a day to day basis, the location of the hotel was just ideal, a five minute walk to the metro and we could access anywhere in Seoul, yet coming back at the end of the day, the area was quieter, less rushed and felt more open than the city.

We didn't eat within the hotel, breakfast seemed a little pricey, and there were plenty of places to eat within a 5 minute walk; there is a particularly good bakery with a stall within the metro station and a number of 'chain' bakeries en route to the metro, burger joints, ice cream parlours and traditional Korean restaurants.  There is also a large EMart just up the road from the hotel, a couple of minutes, if that, where you can pick up snacks or sit down at the fried chicken outlet within the store.

In the end, we were SO pleased that an inadvertent mouse click had brought us to the Four Points in Guro, because we were very happy with the hotel, the location, the facilities and the staff who, throughout our stay, were friendly, welcoming and professional.  Their standard of English was really high (much higher than my Korean!) and they were very helpful in giving advice as to the best way to get to the airport and then making arrangements for us, even coming out to the taxi and helping load up our luggage.

After a day in the city and travelling on the busy metro, it was something of a relief to return to the quieter suburbs of Guru and the space and light of the hotel.  We would certainly stay again.

리뷰_2:
We've just had 9 nights at this lovely little boutique hotel. Although it is not in central Seoul we were at most 30 minutes by subway to just about all the attractions Seoul has to offer.
Our room was clean and comfy, with a little enclosed deck. Even though we had a construction site next door, the double glazed windows meant we didn't hear a thing! Excellent water pressure and good hot water.
The staff were lovely, very helpful indeed.
Given we stayed for more than 7 nights we were entitled to 1 free laundry service, which was very welcome!
The hotel itself is about a 7 minute walk from Dangsan Station, which is the inner circle line, which links up with all the other subways very conveniently. Exit via Gate 13 and head to the main road and turn right. Walk till you come to the first pedestrian crossing, cross over and keep heading right. You will pass a Paris Baguette cafe. Take the next turn left, walk about 50 metres and you will see the entrance to the hotel on the left. There is a little outdoor sitting area. 
The are a lot of eateries around this area. Don't worry if you can't read anything in English on the door - as soon as you walk in you will be passed an English menu😁. W ate along the main road nearly every night, and at a different restaurant too. The options were great, and food always tasty! 
If you want a meal a little more upmarket I can highly recommend Entas (South Korea, Seoul, Yeongdeungpo-gu, 93-1, TCC센터 3층) which is about 15 minutes down Seongyudong 2-ro. Turn left out of the hotel and keep going until you hit a major road then turn left. There is a building that has a small lot of stairs. Go inside and take the lift to the first floor. It has separate dining rooms which are really private and cozy.

I had a 5 days, 4 nights stay in ACUBE Hotel Dongdaemun in July 2019. I must say that this hotel had been a very good one for female solo travelers like me. 

I arrived Seoul at around 9AM and check-in was supposedly not until 3PM. When I did my online reservation, I had made a special request for an early check-in and the hotel was gracious enough to give my request and checked me in as soon as I arrived. The free room upgrade was also a lovely bonus!!

With this being my second time in Seoul, I purposedly chose to stay in the Dongdaemun area as the Myeongdong area was too busy and touristy for me. And I'm glad I chose this neighborhood as it is quiet and more laid-back but has almost everything within arm's reach! 

>> There are 2 airport shuttle terminals (2-5 minute walk)
>> A convenience store at the corner
>> 2 banks and fruit stands within the same street
>> An entire lane of money exchange stalls nearby
>> Blue Bus Terminals around the area (2 minute walk)
>> Exit 7 of Dongdaemun Design History and Culture Park Station (thru the Euljistar Mall) which connects you all the way to Exit 1 of this subway station and brings you to the Green (Line 2) , Blue (Line 4), and Purple (Line 5) lines.
>> A chicken & beer place at the corner by rhe convenience store. 

It is also very close to Gwangjang Market Place and Dongdaemun Design Plaza/History and Culture Park (both about 5 to 10 minutes away by foot).

The rooms are very clean. The bed is queen-sized and soft (foam and not spring). The room is spacious for one traveler. The bathroom is spacious enough for the size of an Asian woman but the bath is a little bit small and cramped up in space. However, I love how clean the bathroom is and how the toilet seat is automated with controls for bidet, dryer, and seat heater.

Breakfast was nothing exceptional but was good enough. I noted that they alternated the menu every 2-3 days.

Internet wifi was fast and uninterrupted.

The staff were easy to talk to as they understood English (but you might have to speak slowly). In particular, I appreciated the kindness of Seol Kim and Jay (both receptionists).

I am glad to have chosen this hotel for my first trip alone. The place definitely lives up to its slogan --- accessible, affordable, and amiable. I will definitely recommend this place to family and friends who will visit Seoul and will definitely come back here on my next visit to Seoul.
리뷰_7:
Just about everything is great about this hotel:

* Very clean rooms. The term "spotless" would apply
* Very comfortable beds
* Modern, clean interior
* High quality breakfast
* Very helpful staff

We stayed in a Family Triple room for four nights and appreciated having separate beds for each of our kids while still having enough room to walk. The bathroom was also a nice size and the sink was outside of the toilet and shower area, which allowed someone to use the sink while someone else was in the toilet or shower. All hotels should be designed that way.

The breakfast is excellent. While somewhat limited in size, the items are very high quality. I liked that there are a mix of types of foods. Western breakfasts tend to be high on sugar and fat, so the fact there was salad and some cooked meat (protein) was wonderful. Maybe others find these dishes odd at breakfast but I welcomed them. And the croissants ARE very good and baked fresh there.

The staff was very helpful whenever we needed them. 

The only downside to staying here is the fact there are not many food options nearby. In a city where there are so many street food stalls, bakeries, and other quick food options, it's disappointing that there really isn't anything quick that is close by to the Acube Hotel. You have to walk 10 minutes a tall office building that has a Tous Les Jours on the ground floor and some food places in the basement. The other option is to order delivery food, but that takes an hour or so to arrive. Our first full day we made the mistake of coming back to the hotel before eating dinner (two of us were tired and just wanted to rest), which meant that the other two had to venture out to find food, which is tough to find in the area around the hotel. 

The metro station is about a 5-minute walk. The area was very quiet at night and we had no problem getting a good night's rest.

Location: Located about a five minute walk from Myeongdong station exit 10. That's about a 10 minute walk from the Myeongdong shopping street so it's very convenient for folks who plan to do a lot of shopping like I did. The hotel is sandwiched between a Kia Motors which you'll most likely see first before seeing the hotel since it's bright orange and then behind the hotel is a Kiswel which is taller than the hotel itself. The hotel isn't quite on the main road so it may be easy to miss - in my first night arriving I ended up walking in from the back side (downhill) versus from the main street (uphill).

Reception and staff: Upon arrival the staff at the front desk at the title was very nice and even asked how my flight was. It's a small gesture but it's very appreciated. The reception staff also helps with the breakfast prep and serving in the morning so if you arrive before 9 a.m. and don't see anyone behind the desk, make sure to check the dining area because that's where they're most likely be. A couple actually arrived at 8:30 in the morning and went up to the second floor right when I left my room and I had helped redirect them back to the first floor. On another occasion it was a cold evening so the AC has been turned off but as a result the power button has been blinking red non-stop despite trying to turn it on and off. This became extremely distracting as I'm the type of person who can only sleep in a pitch-black environment. So I reached out to the lobby and all they could not find a fixed immediately they did offer a short-term solution which was covering the button with black tape and that was all I needed so thank you. 

Room: My room was 202. The room was extremely spacious for a single person. I was able to fully open my carry-on, lay out a duffel bag, open my backpack, dry my umbrella and still have plenty of space to walk around. In the room you'll find a refrigerator, a safe, an AC unit (which can only be turned on or off; you need to contact the lobby to adjust the temperature), a hot water kettle and some of the other more obvious things such as a desk, TV, stool etc. Note the room setup indicates that you need to take off your shoes upon entering as the floor level is higher than the entrance. I discovered that when it gets cold the hotel can set up heated floors so we want to keep the floors clean from dirty outside shoes. 

Two things I didn't like about those room goes that I was located right in front of the elevator so I can pretty much hear when people talk in the hallway. Halfway through my stay I believe a family moved in they talk really loud (as do their rowdy children). Also, the room has a night light from where you insert the key that does not shut off. As I said previously I sleep best when it's pitch black and the night light is pretty bright but I've learned to deal with it in the last week I've stayed here. Luckily the curtains are near blackout status which means only a little light comes in but overall it's doing his job pretty well.

Bathroom: One huge thing I appreciate about this hotel is that there is a shower curtain to keep water from splashing everywhere while you shower.  Upon check-in you will be offered a hair dryer and a wall adapter but make sure you return it during check-out. Per previous reviews, the towels (2) provided were equivalent to a hand or hair towel size at best however I brought my own to use. The towels will be replaced and the bottled water provided will be replenished daily. There are two sets of sandals in the room, one  pair for the bathroom (the one with the little balls for therapeutic purposes I believe and can be used in the shower) and another pair for generally used in the room. 

Toiletries: Aside from your general hand soap, shower gel, shampoo and conditioner there really isn't that much there. You need to supply yourself with your own toothbrush and toothpaste, shower cap if you use one and everything else. You may also request additional clothes hangers from the lobby if needed but must be returned during check-out. 

Laundry: It cost 2500 wash and 2500 drying however the machines are not operated so you must pay the front desk and they will help you operate it and provide you with both detergent and fabric softener. They typically have both machines running to wash and dry the towels so it's best to give them in advance notice so they can clear them out for you. The weird part about this whole system was that washing takes 90 minutes and drying takes 30 minutes which is kind of backwards (past experience with other hotels take 30 mins to wash and 60-90 mins to dry) but it does the job. You can either time it yourself and come check the laundry or the front desk can also call you when your wash is complete and you have to move it into the dryer and when you're dry is done and you can pick up your clothes.

Breakfast: Yes, the breakfast was excellent and above and beyond for a budget hotel. It's a mini buffet consisting of: yogurt + basic toppings, japchae, bacon, sausage, scrambled eggs + ketchup, kimchi, rice balls, daily soup (varies) tteokbokki, toast or bun, 3 types of cereal and milk, OJ, and coffee. Ironically, this was the first time I had tteokboki in Korea and came to love them (ones from the States left a bad impression on me). Breakfast is from 7-9 a.m. and guests receive 20% off the cafe.

The one big issue that I had with this room and hopefully it's limited to this room was that the bathroom smelled funky. As soon as I entered the first night, I couldn't make out what it was or where it was from but it was rank. That night I immediately purchased an air freshener. Soon after I discovered it was from the bathroom and kept the door shot whenever I'm present and the room smelled okay (FYI this smell has nothing to do with #2's bc it was already there when I showed the first night and onwards)... Maybe it's a wet shower thing?

Wonsville review

I cancelled 2 bookings before finally settling for this one. I am glad that I found it. Here are the things that my parents and I love:

- close to both Chungmuro exit 3 and 4 and Myeongdong stations. I prefer Chungmuro because it's on the same side of the street as the hotel.
- our room has a clear view of the Namsan tower. It's beautiful both day and night. We were near the road so we could hear the vehicles. 
- the staff are friendly and helpful. They speak good english. Upon check in, they will ask you if you need a hairdryer and an adapter. These have no extra cost. 
- there's an electric kettle in the room. My dad's a coffee lover so this is a huge plus. There were only complimentary tea bags. You need to bring your own instant coffee. 
- breakfast has variety and absolutely delicious. The cafe/restaurant has a cozy ambiance. Please try the Factoreal sandwich. It's really good. 
- water pressure is good. There are no issues with the hot and cold shower. There's liquid shampoo, bath gel and bath soap provided. Please bring your own toothpaste and toothbrush. 
- the bed and pillows are soft. We had no issues sleeping. The sheets had stains but we didn't mind. 
- check out was a breeze. 

The price that we paid for 3 adults was a bargain. I won't hesitate to stay here again.  

Some tips:
- If you're taking the airport limousine bus, alight at the Myeongdong station. You need to cross the street near the Sejong hotel. 
- If you're taking the train, alight at the Chungmuro station exit 3. You need to walk a few meters to get to the hotel. It's on the same side of the road.

This is a cozy home for travellers who prefer the simpler and quieter side of lodging in Seoul, South Korea.

THE OWNERS
Jin and Andrew are well-experienced hosts and have received wonderful reviews from guests around the world. I decided to stay here because of a friend's good feedback on their services.

THE ROOMS & SALA
The house is protected by CCTVs, sensors and an electronic door lock system. You have access to free internet, TV and a workspace with a printer. It is air-conditioned, good for a summer stay. At the same time, it has heated floors, perfect for the winter season.

THE KITCHEN
The shared kitchen has all the basic things you need. You can store your food in the fridge and cook for your own. Just don't forget to clean up as you go. For self-service breakfast, they provide you with cereal, bread, cup noodles and coffee. 

TOILETS
The shared toilets are stocked with free soap, shampoo and towels. I had fun testing all the Korean products they had. For your laundry, you can freely use their washing machine and detergent.

TERRACE
The rooftop terrace has a table, benches and a BBQ grill, best used during the summer time.

LOCATION
The Hongdae neighbourhood is known for its youthful and artistic atmosphere. It is lined with lively restaurants, quaint cafes, clubs, galleries, fashion shops and creative street art.

I love how the streets transform at night, with food and shopping stalls taking over the lanes. 
The best part is the overload of good-looking young students. 

The guest house is one block away from the main gate of Hongik University.
It is nestled midway up a hill, a good 2-3 minutes exercise (best done after gorging on street food on the way home). Sadly, the hike may not be handicap-friendly.

GETTING THERE
Getting there is easy because both airports, Incheon (AREX All Stop Train) and Gimpo, are connected to the subways that directly passes by the Hongik University Station. The owners offer free pick-up and drop-off in that station. For a fee, you can also reserve a pick-up from the airport. 

3 THINGS I LOVE ABOUT THE HOUSE
1.	The cleanliness and convenience - they clean the rooms everyday and the owners are on-call to help you anytime.
2.	The ambiance - it's peaceful and quiet… until a group of noisy guests come along.
3.	The area - it's a shopping and eating haven. Everything is walking distance, including the subway.

I would definitely return to this guest house if given the chance!

Gloryinn is a great place to stay in Seoul

Pros : 
Location : The hotel is on a major street with multiple subway and bus options nearby. The area feels quite safe. Not too noisy at night. Most top 10 attractions are within walking distance (30-40 min) if you prefer walking to get a sense of the city atmosphere. Two major markets are also nearby -Gwangjang   and Dongdaemun. 
Its squeaky clean including linen
The breakfast is good although basic
The rooms are fully functional and comfortable although small
The staff are super helpful and speak good English
Wifi is good with individual router for each room
Transit from and to airports is pretty
straightforward with just one change needed via subway. There is also a direct bus from Incheon airport
More than five grocery/convenience stores in the near vicinity for the basic needs most of which open till late.
LED tv with few English channels - I could watch popular movies and WWE !

Cons:

The washroom is quite small. The shower and washbasin have a common tap with a rotating knob allowing one to switch between the two. If you forget to turn the knob after the shower there is a risk of getting drenched if you need to use the basin just before leaving the room. I guess that's why they have a hair dryer in every room- to help you quickly dry up!

There is limited space for luggage and few cloth hooks. 

The common remote control for TV and Air conditioner is in Korean. It needs one to refer to a placard  to get familiar to. 

But none of these are dealbreakers.
All in all its a great place to stay and enjoy your sojourn in Seoul.

I thought I've left a review already but oh well.

A great little hotel with friendly and multilingual staff conveniently located near Changdeokgung, Changgyeonggung, Jongmyo Shrine, Bukchon Hanok and Insadong street. A short walk from Anguk and Jongno 3 (Sam) ga stations. If you've got strong legs, you can walk to Gwanghwamun! For the hungry people there's a very small eatery on-site, but the are loads of other options nearby. Free breakfast for all customers - only bread, hard boiled eggs, fish cake and bananas, but good to get you started for the day! My double room was spacious, but no bathtub or shower screen (the toilet will get wet). Free laundry service (not drying though) but haven't used it. Heated flooring for winters and they can help you book a taxi. There's a refrigerator, but way too small!
Would be great if staff could pre-translate the aircon remote - I used google translate which does the job...
I would certainly book this place again if I revisit Seoul.

We had a room on the 5th floor, the room was small (as expected in a major Asian city) but we had room enough for our two hand luggage cases to both be open on the floor throughout our stay. 
Bathroom was a wet room but the fan was pretty good so the water cleared quite fast. 
Shower amenities provided, and towels. 
We had room cleaning once during our stay where the room was freshened up and we were given clean towels, and new bottles of water in the fridge. 

We also borrowed an adaptor from the front desk for a 10,000w deposit which we were given back when we checked out. 

All in all i would definitely recommend the Petercat if you are looking for a no frills, clean and super quiet hotel in a brilliant location. 
Insadong was our favourite area of all! 
Thanks for a great stay!

I like that it has a mini-lamp and wall sockets for charging your devices, as well as, for when I need to do some last minute research on my itinerary the next day.  

The other guests were polite and though I stayed in a room with 7 more people, we didn't really see much of each other.  

As for securing your valuables, they give you a key for the locker underneath the bunk beds to store your luggages and laptop. 

There is also a rule not to do packing late at night so as not to disturb other guests who would be retiring early (if I can remember correctly).  It's not an issue so I usually just prepare my pajamas on my bed before leaving in the morning so I can comply to the rule. 

The bathroom and toilet was clean and they provide small towels for use.  

Breakfast was basic and enough to start your day and you clean after you're done.  At some point, one of the staffs was already cooking their lunch  and she offered me to try a bowl of Kimchi Soup.  (thank you!)

Extra points because location is only 5 mins away from Hongik University Station Exit 3, 3 mins away from Gyeongui Line Forest Park, 10 mins away from Hongik Shopping district on normal pace.

I met some very nice people during my stay and even went out to Namdaemun and Myeongdong with them.  I especially enjoyed the friendliness and hospitality of everyone.  

I highly recommend this place.  Organized, neat, and accommodating.  I would definitely book again. :)

This is a great value for a stay in Seoul. 

The location is absolutely sensational. It's on a street packed with restaurants, with a subway station directly in front of the hotel. Across the street is the entrance to Ikseon-dong Hanok Village, a nest of alleyways with tons of unique shops to explore. Other subway stations are also nearby and Gwangjang market, with its literally thousands of stalls, is a fifteen minute walk. One thing to note is that if you are planning on using a car (you should not be) the streets near the hotel can be almost impassible to vehicles because there are so many people walking around.

The price is an absolute steal for the area, but the hotel is very basic. There is a small lobby and a tiny common area on the second floor with free bottles of water. Rooms are also very minimal. Mine had a bed, TV, nightstand, and not much else. No desk, and only a single outlet. As a final note, the bed and pillows were very firm. I like that, but if you prefer plush mattresses you will find the bed unpleasantly hard.

For a cheap stay where you spend most of your time exploring Seoul rather than being cooped up in a hotel, this is a great choice.
