리뷰_8:
The Standard Hotel is a clean, tidy hotel with good amenities for a city hotel, a very helpful and accommodating staff and a subway station right outside. I wanted to give this hotel 4/5 stars because it wasn't perfect, but the general manager and other employees were so helpful to me every day of my stay that they more than earned the 5th star.

The pros:

_ Phenomenally helpful staff! Every morning, once I had plotted out where my girlfriend and I wanted to go that day, the general manager would take me to the computer, figure out the best way to get to our destinations by subway and print out maps for us. This allowed us to easily travel around Seoul because the city has a well-organized subway system that functions just about flawlessly. Most of the staff spoke very good English.
_ Cheap laundry! The lobby area has two washing machines and two dryers, plus laundry detergent pods, dryer sheets, baskets and bags. Washing costs 4,000 won ($4), and drying is free. The instructions on the machines are written in Korean, but the reception staff can show you what to do. (It's easy, so you'll only need to be instructed one time.)
_ Terrific WiFi! The WiFi was what you'd expect from a hotel in Seoul and was free.
_ Decent size. The room wasn't big, but it also wasn't small. It was a good size for an Asian hotel room. 

A few cons:

_ Breakfast. Breakfast wasn't included, it was $7. But it was worth the $7.
_ Air conditioning. The A/C didn't work during our stay, but they gave us a fan. It was March and was cold outside so we were comfortable in our room with the window ajar and the fan on or with the window closed and the fan on.

Overall, I'd recommend this hotel. I'd stay here again. Our stay was very comfortable and the staff did its best to help us with everything we needed.

TIP: Taxi drivers from Seoul Station seemed to have trouble finding the hotel, even when we had the name and address of the hotel printed out in Korean for them. If you have cellphone access, call the hotel and let the receptionist explain the location to the driver. 

TIP: The hotel's lobby is on the second floor, not on the ground floor. You can take a long staircase up to the second floor or can enter through coffee shop on the ground floor and take an elevator up to the second floor. I think the coffee shop closes around 11 or 11:30 p.m.

TIP: Consider packing fewer clothes and doing laundry one day. It's cheap and fast. You'll need 4,000 won in 1,000-won notes for the washer, and the dryer is free. Detergent pods, dryer sheets and bags for your clothes are free. The washers and dryers are available 24/7 but don't get much use, so don't worry about putting your clothes in at night and picking them up in the morning.

TIP: There's an awesome fried-chicken restaurant, KyoChon, across the street. You must eat there! The original flavor (soy sauce- and garlic-infused) is out of this world, as are the potato wedges, which are crispy on the outside and as fluffy as clouds on the inside. Try the salad with blueberry dressing, too. The restaurant closes at 11 p.m., and the last order is at 10:45 p.m.

TIP: Take advantage of the fact the hotel is next to a subway entrance/exit for the Deungchon station on the 9 line. The subway system is a great way to get around Seoul, and it's affordable and easy to use. The machines that sell tickets have clear English instructions: Pick your destination, insert your money (there are cash change machines nearby usually), get your ticket and go. Signs for approaching trains will say what the next stop is so you'll know if you're going in the right direction. Watch out for express trains, which might skip your stop. When you leave the subway system, remember to put your ticket into one of the machines that refunds 500 won. Take a cellphone photo of a subway map: That's easier to handle than a big folding map.

TIP: The hotel is at a really busy intersection, and it can take 5 minutes or more just to cross the street because you have to cross in two places with traffic lights. As a shortcut, you can use the subway system: Enter at Exit 8 (right in front of the hotel), go down the escalator, follow directions to Exit 1 and come up at Exit 1. You'll be across the street, half a block from the KyoChon fried-chicken restaurant. (I'm pretty sure I have those exit numbers right, but ask the hotel staff or check a subway map. It's very easy.)

TIP: The best way to get to Incheon Airport if you have luggage is by taxi, which costs about 40,000 or 45,000 won (about $40) and takes about 35-40 minutes if there's no traffic. The hotel can arrange for a taxi to pick you up whenever you want. Make sure you ask about traffic conditions around the time you're scheduled to leave because traffic can get bad.

The room is simple, organized and have everything you need - a bathroom, mini fridge, tv air conditioner too. the bathroom is good in terms of size, not too crowded, yet you will have your own space (probably the biggest reason I will return to this hostel). They also have a small common area, where you can get water, or do some small cooking. Laundry is available on site too! 

Nearby the hostel, there are many local food stalls. In the mornings, there are local food stalls selling porridges (red bean or pumpkin), night time there are stalls selling grilled meat or ddokpokki food trucks. They also have a "food street" nearby the subway exit, down the alley you will find lots of local foods, varies from seafood to meat! You have to go down the alley to discover more. Or you can ask the owners/workers from the hostel where they would advise you for meals. A convenient store is down the street too, so don't worry if you want to get some food in the middle of the night. Opposite street of the hostel they have cafes too. (you won't starve for sure in this area).

Hostel is in about 10 minutes or less walking distance to Dongdaemun shopping area, it is convenient for shoppers who want to shop till late night, but don't want to catch a cab ride back to hostel, since it is walking distance. Highly recommended place to stay in Seoul!

Yes, Sieoso Hotel is located on a narrow street not more than 400 meters from Euljiro Sam-ga Station. It's like finding a precious stone amid the most unlikeliest place in Seoul.

My friend and I have stayed at Sieoso for 5 days and 5 nights. The moment we entered the hotel, we were greeted by the receptionist with a welcoming smile despite the fact that it was already early evening when we arrived. With a brief exchange with said receptionist, we're in our room in no time at all.

After we settled in for a while, we noticed that there's water leaking from the sink. Before heading out for dinner, we asked the receptionist if we could transfer to a different room due to the leak. The receptionist immediately apologized for the inconvenience and assured us that he'd have someone fix the problem. Sure enough, the leak appeared as if it wasn't there in the firat place when we returned to our room. I was glad to have experienced such a minor inconvenience because Sieso's action towards it has made me realize how they care about their guests and that's something that will absolutely leave a positive mark on me.

It was winter when we stayed at Sieoso and I appreciate that the hotel's heating system was well managed. The floor of our room was heated as well so it made our stay comfortable. There's warm shower, small refrigerator, spacious closets, metal safe, electric kettle, hair dryer, and generous amount of toiletries in our room. By the end of the day and upon returning to our room, we would find it well cleaned and that we were consistently supplied with another couple of bottled waters. The breakfast itself has this wow factor considering it's complimentary.

In totality, Sieoso's facilities, staff, rate, and location just simply make it a wise choice especially when staying in Seoul for several days. If I'd ever travel back to Seoul, I'd be sure to find myself comfortably staying once again at Sieoso Hotel.

The breakfast area is a bit squeezy, but since I walked out to grab my breakkie at Isaac which is just down the street, I'm totally fine with that as well. I would say, it really depends on what your expectations are. 

The location is perfect. Myeongdong station is just a stone throw away. Myeongdong shopping district is just down the street. You can also walk to Euljiro-1-ga station which is located near to Lotte Young Plaza and take a direct train to Hongdae or Ehua for better shopping experience since those places are not as crowded as Myeongdong (especially Ehua, it's my favorite!). Myeongdong station is easily connected to other popular tourist attractions by their metro services as well. 

The room is fully furnished with basically everything, from attached bathroom (with bathtub), fridge, oven (only available in certain rooms if I'm not mistaken), hairdryer, cups, HD TV and so on. I stayed in a queen size bed room for the first stay, and on my second stay, I stayed in a triple deluxe room which has a queen size bed and 2 single beds! We were so surprised when we saw the beds. I rarely sleep well when I travel but I must say I can sleep like a pig when I was in IB Ville! Their beds are really comfortable. 

Free wifi is a big plus point too. There isn't anything like: "Oh our rooms are fully booked today,  you might experience bad connection / you might not be able to connect to our wireless connection etc etc". NO! You will never encounter things like this. 

They have S, M, L towels provided for you. S size towels are face towels, M size towels are not as big as the usual towels and L size towels are the ones that we use normally. S and M towels are provided for free of charge and you can change it at the lobby whenever you want. You are required to pay a dollar or so for the L size towel. Personally, I think the M size towel is good enough for me. 

There is no room service because you are staying in a guest house (not a hotel) and they do provide room service on request, that is, if you are staying more than 3 days (or every 3 days - I don't really remember this clearly). 

The owner, Ray, doesn't look very friendly on first impression, but he is nice. When we asked the staff on where can we get to try live octopus, Ray even offered to bring us there to eat together! When we requested to get an extra key (with the security pass), the staff agreed to let us have it with a deposit of 10,000 won. To be honest, I didn't expect them to pass us the extra key at all. I was really surprised that they can actually do it! Glad that they are so flexible! 

There are 2 washing machines at the basement too, so if you are having a long stay at IB Ville, you can just go down to do your laundry. The washing machines might be in high demand, especially at night though. 

I really enjoyed my stay at IB Ville and I will definitely go back again!

Staying a night in a traditional korean building was extraordinary experience for me, born and bred in Korea. The guesthouse is very conveniently located in the heart of Korea, and about 200m from the main palace Kyoungbokgung. It took me only 15 min to reach Jongro by a mini bus from the guesthouse. I felt quite cozy in the guesthouse and especially loved the the extremely thick blanket! The wooden building is about 100 years old which maintains traditional style using pine wood that support the entire building and the ceiling. One down side is that the doors are made of wood and thin paper, the rooms were not completely sound proof. 

The owner is a knowledgeable local and told us many folk stories in the area which was very interesting(for example, that a former president of Korea stayed in a building that is perfectly located to be elected as per fengsui). He also prepares formal korean breakfast which was very nice. If you ask, you can get good advice on where to eat, go, drink. The owner is very helpful. He also provides Bukchon tour upon request with a small fee. Me and my friend had an amazing time here and hopefully come back soon. I highly recommend this place!

Location was good, near to the subway, Only 3-5 minutes walk from the subway and bus stops, and old city of Seoul. 
If I were to return to Korea, I would definitely stay here again.

Already have been to Bukchon area several times prior to my visit at Hueahn, I thought it'd be good idea to stay a night at a traditional Korean house in the heart of Seoul.  Indeed it was a very good stay and turned out to be even better experience of exploring Bukchon, thanks to Mr. Yoon, the host of the HueAhn Hanok stay.  He gave me a tour of Bukchon town and shared with me historical value of the town, modern changes it went through past century and about today's people in town.

The room was kept very clean and house staff was kind and very attentive.   It was nice change from a bed to Korean style floor with cotton blanket.  I wish there are more places like this in other cities.

During my stay at HueAhn, I chose to go on hiking the Seoul fortress trail which encircles the old Seoul.  I was not allowed to take photos at some area due to security reason, but surely worth it to give it a try as you can see beautiful view of the city from many different sides.

Location, location, location!  This guesthouse is close to so many conveniences for a traveler! 

Our group was me, my husband and our 8-year old and we stayed for 2 weeks.

The airport limo/bus that also loads your luggage stops literally less than five minutes away, making your arrival and departure easy. 

The guesthouse is not hard to find off the main street, and the road to it is quiet and safe to walk even at the latest hours at night.  

There's several bus stops on that main street minutes away, and it's located in between two very close main line subway stations making it extremely convenient to get anywhere in Seoul. 

--The room--
 
The room was much more than we expected!  It was extremely clean, dust-free, bug-free (and this coming from someone who obsessively looks for spiders lol) and very bright. 
 
The beds were surprisingly comfortable, we had one large bed and a small bed for our daughter and everyone slept really well with plenty of room. Because it was March, it was still a bit chilly out so the heated floors made the room warm to come back to after the long days spent walking.

There was also a rooftop area where you can sit and have a great view and relax. 

--The area--

There is a convenience store (365 plus) within a hundred yards where you can buy all your junk food, drinks, internet cards, and various little things at any hour of day or night.

Also across the main street, probably a five minute walk away, is a Tomato mart (a grocery store) which is also 24 hours where you can get all manner of fresh veggies, fruits, and fish. 

Any direction you go on the main street from the guesthouse you'll find small clothing shops (sock stores which were our 8 yr old's favorite), restaurants, cafes and little stands selling anything from clothes to street food. 

--Bonus -- 

The guesthouse is probably a 10 minute walk from the daily Dongmyo flea market, that will also lead you to the Seoul folk flea market!

Dongdaemun - 24 hour shopping and street food is only 1-2 subway stops away depending on how much you want to walk,  or just a more entertaining 20 minute stroll away filled with tons of street stands selling everything (shopping, shopping, shopping! lol)
-----

Staying at this guesthouse gave us an awesome experience of the daily culture of Seoul. 

And finally the owners of the guesthouse Woo and Jin. They are some of the nicest people you could ever meet and were so welcoming and helpful for our first time in Korea. First time travelers will be well taken care of here and you will definitely feel like it is your home away from home.

Recently traveled to Seoul with my girlfriend, who was attending a conference in the city for a couple days. We decided against a home stay and went for a guest house, but were immediately stuck on which to choose, as there are many options. My girlfriend kept coming back to the Go Woon Dang Guest House, despite the relatively minute amount of reviews about the property on Trip Advisor (Agoda has plenty though). 

Well, fellow travelers, this is the place to be in Seoul. The hanok guest house is the perfect mix of traditional and modern - which is to say that it keeps the beautiful styling of a traditional inn while allowing for the comforts of free WiFi (which I prefer when traveling) and a hot/cold water dispenser at the ready. We stayed in the Gold Room, which features a private bathroom. The sleeping style is on the floor, with a thin mattress and comfortable bedding. Our room also featured an efficient AC unit (it was hot in June). The room was super clean and was attended to each day while we were out. The other four rooms in the guest house share a public bathroom on the opposite side of the courtyard. I could see this being an issue in the winter for guests, but it's a small price to pay for what you get here.

The room is one thing, but it isn't all that you are getting for your money. First let's discuss the service. Mr. and Mrs. Kim are amazing hosts. Mr. Kim speaks Korean, Mandarin, Japanese and English. His hospitality is through-the-roof good and he assisted us with many things, including recommendations, directions, travel arrangements - and many times he'd relax in the courtyard with us and ask about our time in Seoul. His wife is polite, all smiles, and creates the most amazing breakfasts for guests. It's nice to be able to stay somewhere and have your breakfast included in the price, as well as be something to look forward to each morning. We were sad when we had to leave early in the AM one morning (prior to the 8:30am breakfast service in the common room) and miss a meal. Each morning featured a new style of dish, always traditional and always homemade. Yum! The other member of the family is Kooman, the son. He studied in the US and speaks excellent English. He not only made it a point to meet all of the guests and learn about their lives, but he also assisted us with finding a wonderful restaurant in the area - by escorting us to it personally! He also provided us with an electrical outlet adapter, as we came unprepared.

The location of the guest house was perfect for us. You're only a block away from Gyeongbokgung Palace, and a short walk from the Blue House, Changdeokgung and the Bukchon Hanok Village. Not only that, but the subway entrance is also a short walk away, which can get you to anywhere in city limits - the subway is very easy and efficient in Seoul. It must also be mentioned that a popular dining option is only two blocks away - Tosokchon - that features excellent samgyetang (ginseng chicken soup).

Keep in mind that finding Go Woon Dang was an adventure - we had to ask a friendly gentleman on the street, who was able to direct us with his smartphone. Make sure you know where you're going. Once you find it though, you'll never forget where it sits.

This is a great value and we highly recommend this guest house to any looking to enjoy some time in Seoul. We met guests from Japan, Sweden, China and Hong Kong during our stay. Apparently Go Woon Dang is very popular with oversees travelers. Not only is the property authentic, but also the owners are great ambassadors for the Korean people. We will only stay here the next time we visit this city.

I stayed at this guesthouse for 8 weeks and had an excellent experience. Here are some of the reasons why I think so:
- The location is excellent. It is easy to find and it's very conveniently located, near both Hongdae and Hapjeong stations. What I liked best was that it's not on a "main" road, but a side alley, which makes it a bit quieter than some other guesthouses.

- The owner knows *everything* about Korea and Hongdae and Seoul. I've spent a lot of time in Seoul and I've seriously never met anyone who knows as much as he does. If you have any questions about what to see or how to get around, he can definitely help - and best of all, he's very eager to help. He is very passionate about travel and he loves to see people have a great travel experience.
- There is a cafe/bar/record shop/performance venue on the first floor and so there is almost always *someone* on the first floor hanging out. I met quite a few people down there, which was nice (if you like meeting people.. which I do..) Yes, it's true there are performances downstairs (maybe once a month), but (1) they're actually pretty good, and seeing an indy show in Seoul would make your trip a bit different from everyone else's palace tours, and (2) they're always finished by 10pm so your sleep will not be interrupted. All in all, I think having the lounge downstairs is a total plus. And yes there is a cute pug downstairs, and no, he doesn't pee all over the place.
- There is free breakfast in the morning. It's not fancy but it does the trick. If you've spent any time in Seoul you'll know that it's really hard to get breakfast *any*where, so it's really nice to have some toast, cereal, coffee, and juice waiting for me downstairs.

We wanted a hanok experience for our week long holiday in Seoul, and we chose Irang after looking at many many options.

Some of our considerations:

1) We wanted to rent the entire hanok (or an annex) instead of only 1-2 rooms.  Hanok walls are paper thin, so if you share adjoining rooms with strangers, you will need to keep your volume down.  After watching a few you-tube videos of guests whispering (and I really mean whispering) to each other, we decided that entire hanoks were the way to go.
2) Access to bathrooms and toilets from the main house (or rooms).  Korean winters are bitterly cold and we did not fancy having to dress up and step outside just for a visit to the loo.
3) No hanoks located on high grounds.  While the view may be fantastic, the daily walking up slope is not fun.
4) Close to subway and eateries
5) English speaking host

Irang had ticks in all the right boxes, and was just perfect!

Our host, Jacqueline, was charming and went out of her way to help us.  She responded to all our questions (before and during the stay) very promptly.  In fact she provided better service than the official 1330 travel hotline.  Thumbs up!

The ondol heated floors were heavenly after a whole day's outing.  Although the futons looked thin, we found them very comfortable and had no backaches at all.

The hot/cold water dispenser was very useful.

TV channels were all in Korean language, but my kids enjoyed the cartoons nevertheless.

A great stay.  Do try it!

리뷰_2:
My second time back at Jin Guesthouse and it's still as perfect as I remembered it to be! 

So starting off w the location, it's perfect. It's located at Chungmuro Stn, which is just a few stops away from the shopping places (Itaewon, Myeongdong, Dongdaemun) and is easily accessible to other places (a change or 2 of the subway lines and you can get to places like Hongik Uni, Yeouido, World Cup Stadium etc). The guesthouse is a few mins away from the station, depending on whether you get off at the right exit (Exit 3 if you're getting off from Subway Line 3 or Exit 2 if you're getting off from Subway Line 4). 

So to those who are actually planning to go there, here's my directions for you guys: upon exiting from the subway line, walk straight down the path where you'll see outlets like Popeyes, Dunkin' Donuts, Tom Tom Coffee etc. Just before the movie theatre, you'll see a small alleyway. Walk through that alleyway and you're bound to see the words Jin Guesthouse!

The house is very clean, despite the no. of guests that they've got staying there and the fact that the only one who does the cleaning is the nice lady, Mrs Lee. The toilets are always spick and span and the room is neat and tidy. 

I'm not sure about the other rooms but I managed to stay in 2 diff rooms cos of my 2 separate trips there - the family room and the 8-bed dorm room (which we got all to ourselves). my experiences w e rooms so far is that it's pretty spacious! the 8-bed dorm room was more than enough for the 5 of us staying in the room and the family room was more than enough for me and my friend! the rooms consisted of beds and a coat stand, which provides for ample space to move around and dump your shopping bags like anywhere in the room!

there's no private toilet and shower rooms, its for everyone to share. but if you're afraid of it being dirty, trust me, your fears are unfounded! it's so clean, i didn't feel disgusted or uncomfortable using the amenities at all! i dare say, its one of my most comfortable experiences using the toilets/shower than my experiences in hotels. again, wake up early if you're planning to bathe, or you'd have to wait in line cos there will be people bathing (erm, just to get this out there: there's the female shower room and there's the male shower room). 

breakfast is pretty simple. you've got your usual instant coffee or tea, which you gotta make yourself. there's butter/jam and bread, which you can choose to toast if you want to. occasionally, there's eggs (either hard-boiled or scrambled).

my fav place in the house would be the main hall. there's the TV in there (sometimes Mrs Lee would be watching her shows) and 3 computers for you to use. it's a pretty good place to meet some of the other guests staying in this house! i met 2 australians, an american lady, a taiwanese girl and some fellow Singaporeans so its a good opportunity to mingle and get to know people from all walks of life! 

now, the service provided by hyungseok and his mother was top-notch. we arrived at the guesthouse at 10am, which is 2 hours ahead of check-in time but we were allowed early check-in, which was very kind of them, considering e fact that my family and i were running on zero-sleep after a long flight. my uncle had some knee pain and mrs lee kindly gave us some medicinal plaster to help relieve his pain. it was really an appreciated gesture, considering the fact that she didn't have to do that.

oh, they've got a cute little dog, which is kept outside. it can be a good or a bad thing, depending on whether you love dogs or not. i basically am no animal lover, i'm scared of animals so yes, the dog was basically the damper. dont get me wrong, it's totally harmless and actually super adorable and very friendly, but it kept coming towards me and being scared of animals means that i do not appreciate having animals being close to me. but it listens to instructions so if you gesture for it to sit, it will sit (altho for a while).

리뷰_1: If you want to experience staying in a typical Korean house, this is the right place specially because of the house owners who made me feel like at home. As traditional Korean houses, the rooms are around a yard and despite they are relatively small are comfortable and everything is clean.  This experience made me think at coming to Korea again. The owners are charming and helped me all the time for anything I needed. The only thing is the first time it is hard to find the house if you arrive there at night.
리뷰_2: My wife and I stayed here for 6 nights while visiting Korea and had a fantastic time. The hosts were friendly, kind and helpful. They went out of their to way to make sure we were comfortable and enjoying our stay in Seoul. For example they provided us with an extra mattress and guided us to a local ginseng chicken soup restuarant and helped us order. The rooms were spotless and the traditional mattress on the floor was surprisingly comfortable. The hanok is also in a great neighborhood - it's a 10 minute walk to the Hyehwa metro station and the #8 bus stops 2 mins away that takes you right there. It was really nice to be outside of touristy Bukchon and in a genuine residential neighborhood. The area around Hyehwa station is filled with restaurants and theatres and so is full of good places to eat at night. Be warned though hanok rooms are small and you are sleeping on a mattress on the floor so if you need the amenities of typical hotel a hanok stay may not be for you. But if you are interested in a genuine cultural experience in a place that feels safe and comfortable with wonderful and kind hosts then I'd recommend Eugene's House for sure. The traditional breakfasts of home made pickles and different soups or rice porridge were terrific. Our stay really gave us a unique window into Korean life that we are so grateful for.
리뷰_3: I stayed at the Eugenes house in Seoul with my three teenage kids for two nights. We felt very welcomed into this house,the owners was a very nice family!, And if you want to stay the korean way, this is the perfect place! We were SO well taken care of, and it became an experience we will never forget.It was clean,nice,charming and very safe. I will definetly stay there the next time I go to Seoul.
리뷰_4:
What an amazing experience.  My husband and I took our children, and we had rooms RF1 and RF2.  Be forewarned.  This is not a typical north american hotel.  If you have back problems best to find a large chain hotel.  BUT, if you're up for adventure and want to enjoy traditional Korean culture, then Eugene's is a gem.  Our room was smaller than tiny.  We had heated floors and very thin mats.  Our children stayed in an adjoining room separated by a sliding rice paper door.  The bathroom was a hoot!  Basically a powder room with a shower head above the sink.  But super heating turbo fan dried everything up quickly.  
Our hosts went out of their way to make us feel welcome, serving us tea when we arrived, introducing us to their friends (who wanted to brush up on their english!) and hosting a Korean breakfast the next morning.  The proprietress is fascinating and quite a history buff.  She has an amazing collection of traditional Korean outfits that the children tried on.  Eugene's is well located with shopping, theatre and amazing restaurants near by.  Take a chance - it's an experience of a lifetime!
리뷰_5:
I recently stayed 3 nights at Eugene's House and would not hesitate to stay again next time I'm in Seoul.  The house and antique furnishings were beautiful.  It is set just off the beaten track, but within a few minute's walk of a lively student area (Daehangno), which is jam-packed with restaurants, bars, cafes, some shops and lots of small theatres.  It is also close to all the main tourist sites, by foot or metro (Hyewha station is 10mins walk away).

I chose the smallest room, but from what I saw, some of their other rooms are decent-sized.  The sleeping mats on the floor were not much harder than mattresses in Korean hotels, so it didn't affect my sleep at all. The host family are really friendly and happy to arrange cultural activities for guests.  On my first night, knowing I was a solo traveller, the lady owner invited me along to where her family were having dinner (a place that has the most delicious mandu dumplings ever!) and on my second day, a Korean teacher came to give me and another guest a language lesson.

Breakfast was the best out of the places I stayed - soft bread; different rice porridge, side dishes and traditional tea each morning.

Anyone looking for a true Korean experience should choose Eugene's House.
리뷰_6:
I returned to this guesthouse again (having stayed here last year), same small room, but double mattress, and so welcoming. I was only booked in two nights at the beginning of my stay and one night at the end, as the plan was to visit the DMZ from here for one day then travel elsewhere in Korea. Barely had I put my bags down than they had a hands on kimchi making session, and a couple of days later, just as I was leaving a troupe of musicians turned up to play the traditional korean harp with drum accompaniement, followed by Korean snacks. The courtyard was stuffed full of guests, friends and others, but unfortunately I had to leave for the train station just as the party was getting going.
When I returned for my last night a week later, I was presented with a bag of the kimchi I had helped prepare (which fortunately survived the flight home).
리뷰_7:
This is a traditional Korean guest house, so small rooms and thin mats on the floor to sleep on, but ask for more mats if they are to thin. The house is stuffed full of antiques from Korea and China, and in a quiet area, off the main tourist track but still very close to lots of good eating areas around Hye Wha and the University, and easy transport links. And free Wifi to track cancelled flights and volcanoes
I should only have been there three days, but then a volcano erupted in Iceland, and on returning to the guest-house unexpectedly the owners really were very kind, and flexible. Try something Korean.
리뷰_8:
